symptom: ako/mxcli#1516 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1606): `actionbutton b (Caption: 'Ping', Action: call microflow M.Ping())` failed `mxcli check` with `mismatched input ')' expecting the start of a statement`, while `call microflow M.Ping();` parses in a flow body and the widget action parsed without the brackets. Same error for call nanoflow, show page, the deprecated microflow/nanoflow/show_page spellings, a microflow or nanoflow DataSource, OnClick, OnChange, a pluggable widget's action property, `alter page set Action`/`set DataSource`, and a navigation or menu-document item's OnClick. `use fragment Hdr()` was worse: no error at all without a project
cause: microflowArgsV3 (MDLPage.g4) required at least one argument, `LPAREN microflowArgV3 (COMMA microflowArgV3)* RPAREN`, and every one of those sites reaches it through actionExprV3 or dataSourceExprV3. The optional rule failed on `( )`, the widget's property list then met `(` and recovery blamed the `)`. fragmentArgs had the same shape, but there the page body's generic widget alternative (`widgetTypeV3` ends in IDENTIFIER, and widgetPropertiesV3 MAY be empty) re-read `use fragment Hdr()` as a widget of type `use` named `fragment` plus a widget of type `Hdr` with `()` as its properties, so check without -p passed and check -p said '`use` is not a widget in this project' (MDL-WIDGET25)
fix: Both rules take an optional list inside the brackets, like workflowCallArguments and the flow-body callArgumentList already did. No visitor change: buildMicroflowArgsV3 and buildFragmentArgs return nil for no children, so `X()` builds the statement `X` builds. Purely additive (a refused script now parses), so no mdl-version gate. describe still writes no brackets
test: mdl/visitor/visitor_empty_call_args_test.go: 23 sites, each X() vs X compared as whole statements plus deprecation codes, with a non-empty argument list as the control that must differ. Reverting the grammar (patch out, make grammar) fails all 23: 22 as parse errors and use fragment on statement equality, since it parsed as two widgets. Real 11.13.0 app (mdl-examples/bug-tests/widget-action-1516-empty-call-args.mdl): a page written with () and its bracket-less twin store identical BSON once $ID and the page name are set aside, describe identically, describe -> exec reports Unchanged, mx check 0 errors
insight: One shared rule carried eight alternatives (six actions, two data sources) into every site that takes an action or a data source, which is the argument for auditing by rule rather than by the reported spelling: grep for the rule name, not the keyword. Compare WHOLE statements between X() and X, not the Args field: an empty-but-present mapping list, or an alternative that silently matched something else, both show up there, and a control (a real argument list must change the statement) proves the comparison can see a difference. A rule that cannot match does not always produce a parse error: when a generic fall-back alternative exists (here an unknown widget type with an optional empty property list) the input is re-read as something else and `check` without a project passes, so a site that 'parses' at baseline still needs the AST checked. `use building block X()` and `snippetcall (Params: ())` stay errors on purpose: they are an override list and a property map, not an argument list, and the messages already name what is expected
